headline: Six killed as Israeli strike hits surgery ward at Gaza hospital
standfirst: An overnight military strike on the Nasser Medical Complex in southern Gaza has killed six people, marking the deadliest single attack since recent elections.
keyPoints: Six people were killed during an overnight strike on the surgical building at Nasser Hospital.
The Israeli military stated the target was a local Hamas commander and other fighters.
Hamas denied utilising the medical facility for military operations.
The incident occurred despite a wider ceasefire agreement brokered by the United States.

paragraphs: An overnight military attack struck the surgical department of the Nasser Medical Complex in the southern Gaza city of Khan Younis. Local medical authorities confirmed that six individuals died and nearly thirty others sustained injuries in the blast. The incident represents the highest single-day death toll from a military strike since Israel held elections last month.

Fighter jets targeted a building housing surgical wards and intensive care units without advance warning, according to hospital officials and paramedics at the scene. Footage from the location revealed extensive structural damage, including a partially collapsed exterior staircase and debris scattered across internal corridors. Several medical staff members, patients, and people accompanying them were among the casualties.

The armed forces of Israel verified the operation, stating that the objective was a high-ranking commander from the local brigade alongside other combatants. Officials asserted that the site functioned as a command hub used to direct operations against troops and civilians. Meanwhile, separate incidents across the territory brought the total daily fatalities to eleven people following various drone and gunfire events.

sections.heading: Context of hospital targeting
paragraphs: The Nasser Medical Complex serves as the largest healthcare facility in southern Gaza, providing essential care to a population nearing one million residents. Medical infrastructure throughout the territory has suffered extensive damage since hostilities began following the October 2023 attacks led by Hamas. International agencies note that healthcare buildings possess protected status under global conventions.

Despite this designation, medical installations have experienced repeated bombardments throughout the ongoing conflict. Health authorities report that the facility in Khan Younis has faced multiple strikes over the past three years. This ongoing destruction has severely crippled local medical services while displacement camps suffer from flooding caused by recent heavy rains.

sections.heading: Conflicting statements from officials
paragraphs: Representatives for the military defended the operation by claiming that armed groups deliberately exploit civilian infrastructure to hide operatives and store weaponry. They maintained that precautions were taken before executing the precise engagement against the targeted commander. However, hospital directors strongly rejected these claims and denied that the compound served any military purpose.

Political representatives and international bodies voiced deep concern over the mounting civilian toll. A regional peacekeeping board lamented the continuous loss of life and urged the immediate implementation of broader diplomatic frameworks. Without urgent intervention, observers warned that civilian populations will continue bearing the ultimate cost of ongoing military actions.

sections.heading: Broader regional impact
paragraphs: The latest escalation unfolds against a backdrop of fragile political transitions and an existing truce arrangement. Although a United States-brokered ceasefire took effect late last year, regular military engagements continue to affect various parts of the enclave. Thousands of casualties have been recorded since the formal cessation of major hostilities was declared.

The humanitarian crisis has deepened significantly due to restricted access for international organisations and damaged infrastructure. Verification of ground events remains challenging as outside media outlets face entry restrictions. Local ministry figures, which are widely accepted by international observers, continue tracking the rising human cost of the protracted conflict.

sections.heading: Outlook and upcoming developments
paragraphs: Political instability within the national government adds further complexity to ongoing military strategies in the region. Caretaker leadership continues to manage security operations while coalition discussions remain unresolved. Observers expect military operations to persist periodically despite international calls for restraint and adherence to humanitarian protocols.

Future developments will likely depend on international diplomatic pressure and the enforcement of existing truce terms. Aid agencies emphasize the urgent need to safeguard remaining medical facilities from further destruction. Ensuring the protection of patients and medical personnel remains critical as humanitarian conditions across the territory deteriorate further.
